recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Reintroducing prose about retired CarePlan.activity.note or removed plannedActivityDetail structures would be stale; the current source satisfies the seed intent.
issue_request: Published / Persuasive with Modification Patient Care issue requesting additional guidance for CarePlan.activity.note, including that it not describe the activity being performed and that it use Annotation.
initial_application: The Jira comment cites SVN #6766; git-svn commit d6c4981fa8 (build@6766) changed the CarePlan spreadsheet so the old activity note concept became CarePlan.activity.progress, with Annotation type, status/progress wording, and a comment prohibiting use to describe the activity itself.
additional_context: CarePlan is active in the current build. Later CarePlan work removed CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityDetail (FHIR-39101) and then clarified the activity.progress comment to reference only CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityReference (FHIR-48415 / f94dfe3851), explaining why the current wording differs from the DSTU1-era resolution text.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/careplan/structuredefinition-CarePlan.xml defines CarePlan.activity.progress as Annotation, describes it as notes about adherence/status/progress, and explicitly says it should not describe the activity to be performed.

related_jiras.note: Removed CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityDetail, which explains why current activity.progress guidance points only to plannedActivityReference.
Clarified CarePlan.activity.progress and performedActivity wording after the R5 CarePlan refactors.
Renamed CarePlan activity outcome/reference/detail concepts in R5 and is part of the activity terminology history.
